case.summary: The customer reported a $482.12 purchase they did not make, triggering an investigation of four online purchases between $400 and $500 on the same card within about 30 minutes. The pattern matches an undocumented coordinated scheme where similar under-$500 runs appeared on 11 other cards in the surrounding weeks, indicating fraud. The evidence points to fraud and the case was escalated to a fraud analyst after the analyst confirmed the coordinated scheme. The card was blocked, a case was created, connected cards will be monitored, and a report will be filed. The investigation stays open pending further monitoring of the linked cards.

sar.narrative: On November 21, 2016, card C07297-K1 was used for four online purchases totaling $1,906.07, each between $400 and $500 and completed within 30 minutes. The transactions occurred from multiple devices, and the same under-$500 run shape was observed on eleven other cards (C00466-K1, C01890-K1, C02265-K1, C03633-K1, C05423-K1, C05766-K1, C05851-K1, C06881-K1, C10751-K1, C10990-K1, C12641-K2) within ±30 days, indicating a coordinated scheme. The device profiles used were known on the card, but past alerts on these profiles were mostly cleared as genuine customer activity, providing weak support for a legitimate claim. The customer C07297 denied the $482.12 purchase, and the pattern of multiple near-threshold authorizations is consistent with fraud. Because the total exposure exceeds $1,000 and the scheme involves multiple cards, the activity is deemed suspicious. The card was blocked, a case was created, and the linked cards will be monitored. The affected transaction IDs are 3476602, 3476633, 3476665, and 3476682.
